profile.headline: Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, C# / .NET, Blazor | AI-assisted delivery | I own a surface end to end and ship it
profile.summary:
I am a full-stack developer, and front end is where my depth is.

My path in was not a straight line. I started teaching myself to code in 2022, and my first real work was on an AI storytelling app where I owned the UI layer. Since then it has been three and a half years of production work, mostly on small teams where I own a surface end to end.

What that has actually looked like:

On an analytics platform for cannabis retail, I am one of two engineers and a founding team member. I own the UI layer and the external vendor portal, and I moved into back-end work as the product grew: EF Core migrations, role and permission rules, Docker and deployment, and the transaction data pipeline that feeds our semantic layer.

Before that, on a nine-month client engagement, I built internal tools and an AI chatbot over a company's transaction data, and I caught a silent schema change in their exports that would have quietly broken their reporting.

And then there is the work I did alone. Two live Shopify storefronts, five months, no other developer on either account. Fifty custom Liquid sections, a migration off a page builder to native theme sections, and a custom app built in house. I set up the repositories and the version control too, because neither storefront had any.

What I am good at: taking a vague brief and turning it into something that ships, reading data carefully enough to catch what nobody asked me to look for, and learning whatever stack the job actually needs. I have done that four times now, and I am quick at it because I use AI tooling heavily and I know where it helps and where it does not.

I am looking for full-stack or front-end roles where I can own a surface and ship it. If that is what you are hiring for, I would like to hear about it.

positions.title: Contract Developer
positions.description:
A consulting entity I co-founded, run alongside Rival Response.

Greenlight Dispensaries, retainer, Oct 2025 to Jul 2026
One of two developers on a nine-month retainer. I contributed to a dashboard rework, internal tools, and an AI chatbot over the company's transaction data, and worked on the Cube.dev semantic layer and the transaction data feeding it. That was my introduction to Cube.dev, and it is why Rival Response adopted it a few months later. I also caught a silent schema change in the client's transaction exports, where CLIENT_STORE became CLIENT_CODE and then TRANSACTION_CLIENT_ID, and pushed back until the agreed column contract was restored.

Party Patch and InstantIV, Shopify e-commerce, May 2026 to present
Sole developer on two live storefronts for five months, 687 commits, with no other developer on either account. I set up the repositories and version control myself, since neither storefront had any in place.

Work included 50 custom Liquid sections, a migration off Replo to native theme sections, retheming on Dawn, product and navigation architecture, UpCart and Loox integrations, and a custom Shopify app built in house. I was also the primary contact for every request from the client's team, technical or administrative, well beyond the original development scope.

I also built a complete theme to spec for Hiden and a landing page for VitaPop in development stores. Both were reviewed and approved; neither is deployed yet.

positions.title: Software Engineer (Founding Team)
positions.description:
Marketing analytics platform for cannabis retail: attribution and campaign reporting off a Cube.dev semantic layer. Two engineers and an infrastructure partner.

I am the front-end developer and a founding team member. I took the product from prototype to paying customers, and I own the UI layer and the external vendor portal: Blazor Server pages and components, dashboard layouts, navigation, the Tailwind and DaisyUI theme, and the vendor-facing page shell.

I moved into back-end work as the product grew: EF Core migrations and data-sync configuration, role and permission restrictions on administrative accounts, and Docker and deployment setup. I also set up and maintain the transaction data pipeline configuration feeding Cube.dev, including import paths, AWS settings, and market-source handling, plus the integration and data-pipeline documentation.

Stack: .NET 9 modular monolith, Blazor Server, CQRS, SQL Server, Redis, Cube.dev.

positions.title: Developer
positions.description:
Contributed to a voice-and-touch self-service kiosk for a state motor-vehicle service: layout work, touch-input handling, voice-navigation synchronization, and on-screen keyboard behavior, on an AI-assisted flow for title and registration steps.

Sweat equity engagement. The prototype stalled on government procurement and internal communication.

positions.title: Junior Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
Contributed significantly to the development of the "Live Voting App," a dynamic platform designed for interactive voting experiences with live and remote audiences. Specialized in front-end development with occasional full-stack responsibilities.

Key Contributions:

- Front-End Specialization: Played a key role in the front-end development of the Live Voting App, utilizing technologies such as Blazor WebAssembly, Razor template, MudBlazor, and custom CSS.
    
- User Interface Enhancement: Implemented intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for hosts and clients, ensuring a seamless and engaging voting experience.
    
- Questioning System Implementation: Developed the user interface and functionality for versatile questioning, allowing hosts to pose open-ended and multiple-choice questions, customize voting options, and visualize results with different chart types.
    
- Result Display Customization: Contributed to the implementation of result display features, giving hosts the ability to show or hide real-time voting outcomes based on their preferences.
    
- Subscription Management Integration: Collaborated on the development of a subscription page with three tiers, allowing users to access varying levels of features based on their subscription plans.
        
- Full-Stack Collaboration: Engaged in occasional full-stack responsibilities, connecting the front-end components to the persistent database and ensuring seamless data flow between user, room, and questions.
    
- Modularity and Scalability: Contributed to the integration of the Live Voting App as a modular component within a larger system, allowing for future expansion with additional modules for enhanced functionality.
    

This experience enhanced my skills in front-end development within the .NET ecosystem and provided valuable exposure to full-stack responsibilities.
positions.insights: Skills: .NET · Git · Software Development · Software Troubleshooting · Code Refactoring · Debugging · MudBlazor · Front-end Engineering · C# · User Interface Design · Responsive Web Design · User Experience (UX)

positions.title: Junior Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
Played a crucial role in a collaborative team dedicated to realizing a Word Search Generator with playable features website. As the lead front-end developer, I contributed significantly to both the visual and functional aspects of the project, working extensively with the .NET full stack ecosystem, including C#,  Blazor WebAssembly, and MudBlazor as the UI framework.

Key Contributions:

- Holistic Design Involvement: Actively participated in shaping the overall design and flow of the program, ensuring a cohesive and user-centric experience. Engaged in discussions and decisions related to engineering choices, including data structures and the required persistent data in the database.
    
- Interactive Word Generation: Introduced an innovative feature where a random word served as a seed in API calls, dynamically populating associated words and enhancing the depth of word searches.
    
- Customization Capabilities: Implemented user-centric customization options, allowing individuals to personalize their word search experience by choosing different fonts within the puzzles.
    
- Backend Expertise: Extended my role beyond the front end, delving into the backend to implement functionality for checking word occurrences, showcasing a comprehensive understanding of the project's architecture.
    

Despite our progress, the project underwent a pivot before completion, highlighting my adaptability and ability to contribute across multiple facets of the development process.
positions.insights: Skills: C# · Front-End Development · Software Development · .NET · MudBlazor · Software Troubleshooting · Code Refactoring · User Interface Design · Responsive Web Design · User Experience (UX) · SQL Server Management Studio · Databases · REST APIs

positions.title: Junior Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
Played a pivotal role in developing an innovative software solution that seamlessly blended generative AI, storytelling, and interactive decision-making. Led front-end development using HTML, CSS, Razor, and the MudBlazor UI component library within the .NET ecosystem. Collaborated with a cross-functional team from project conceptualization to deployment.

Key Achievements:

- Holistic System Integration: Orchestrated the convergence of generative AI, user decision-making, and MudBlazor UI components, ensuring a seamless and immersive storytelling experience.

- AI-Driven Storytelling:  Contributed to the creation of a dynamic storytelling platform where user decisions shaped the narrative, accompanied by AI-generated images. Involved in developing a system allowing users to save and resume unfinished stories.
    
- End Story Feature: Helped Introduce a unique end-scene mechanism, triggered by user choices or narrative events causing harm to the character. This added a captivating dimension to the storytelling experience.
    
- Token System Implementation: Actively contributed to the design and implementation of a token system, providing users with an initial allocation for story generation. Upon depletion, users had the option to refill tokens to continue generating stories.
    
- Shareable Stories and Image Gallery: Enabled easy sharing of generated stories and curated a gallery showcasing all AI-generated images associated with each narrative.
    

This experience afforded valuable exposure to diverse technologies, including MudBlazor, .NET, and C#, contributing to a comprehensive skill set in full-stack development.
